newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Lebanon eyes banking presence in Romania.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon eyes banking presence in Romania.

text.p: Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said on Wednesday that Beirut was planning to open a private bank in Romania.

"The president of the Lebanese Banks Association is working on plans to set up a private Lebanese-European-Romanian bank," Bouez told reporters after talks with his Romanian opposite number Adrian Severin.
The Lebanese minister declined to identify the partners in the planned bank, but said talks on its creation were at a "very advanced stage".
Some 40 commercial banks operate in Romania. Ten are branches of foreign banks.

Lebanese businessmen, including executives of Beirut's leading bank Fransabank, are accompanying Bouez on a five-day visit which started with the opening of a Lebanese consular office in the Black Sea port of Constanta on Sunday.
Bouez praised the efforts of Romania's centrist government in changing banking and investment legislation to attract foreign investors.
He said Lebanon was interested in investing in Romanian agriculture and industry and urged Bucharest to liberalise post-communist legislation on foreign investment.
The government is discussing changes to the law on foreign investment in keeping with reform pledges made after the leftists ousted ex-communists in last year's elections.
